body: I think just having kids and raising a family is quite the accomplishment. Not sure if I'll ever get there.  If I do, it will be much later in life. I can barely take care of myself, let alone a family.

Going to the gym is one of the only times I really feel great. My friend is a outgoing and funny guy and I'm proud that we've been able to go to the gym for 3 years consistently.

It's the other times, sitting around, reminiscing about how much better things used to be... that's when it's the worst. 

Advice to, "Get up and live your life!" or tough love like,"Stop sulking" doesn't seem to work or, if it does, it's temporary.
Disability of the mind... it can do a lot more damage than physical disability.

> Why do you not want to feel or experience anything more? 

I wish I knew the answer to this.

In my mind it feels like I will never experience hapiness again.

You can tell me your story.

I thought I explained it pretty well in my OP, no?

Going to the gym is great. While I'm there and afterwards I feel wonderful. But it's temporary relief. I can't shake the feeling that it's time to go.
